The coordination endpoint is a mailbox service for agents that do not share a
process. A Pi session reaches it through its `coordination_*` tools. This guide
makes the same calls from R so that every step and every reply is visible.

## Start the endpoint

The endpoint is a Node process that serves SQL methods from ducknng. It owns
one DuckDB file and listens on an `ipc://` socket beside it:


``` bash
node tools/pi-coordination-endpoint.ts \
  "$STATE/coordination.url" "$STATE/coordination.duckdb" > "$STATE/endpoint.log" 2>&1 &
echo $! > "$STATE/endpoint.pid"
until [ -s "$STATE/coordination.url" ]; do sleep 0.1; done
```

Its manifest lists the coordination methods, in the `sql_method` family, next
to ducknng's built-in control methods:


``` r
url <- guide_url()
manifest <- rpc_describe(url)
methods <- Filter(function(m) identical(m$family, "sql_method"), manifest$methods)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  method = vapply(methods, `[[`, "", "name"),
  purpose = vapply(methods, function(m) m$request_schema$description, "")
))
```



|method            |purpose                                                                                          |
|:-----------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|register          |Create or resume one project-scoped agent instance lease                                         |
|heartbeat         |Renew one registration lease and replace its bounded status                                      |
|list_agents       |List live agent instances in the caller's project                                                |
|send              |Durably send one idempotent message to one mailbox, several mailboxes, or every other live agent |
|receive           |Lease a bounded ordered batch from the registered agent mailbox                                  |
|ack               |Idempotently acknowledge a current delivery receipt                                              |
|reserve           |Acquire or renew an advisory project-scoped resource lease                                       |
|list_reservations |List active reservations, optionally only those conflicting with a resource                      |
|release           |Idempotently release an advisory resource lease owned by the caller                              |
|unregister        |End one agent instance without deleting durable mail                                             |



## Mail for an agent that is not running

A mailbox belongs to a stable `(project, agent)` pair, not to a session, so
`alice` can write to `bob` before `bob` has ever started:


``` r
alice <- register("alice")
sent <- rpc_call(url, "send", list(
  registration_id = alice$registration_id,
  recipient_agent_id = "bob",
  idempotency_key = "handoff-1",
  content = "Review the draft.\nReply with one sentence."
))
show(sent, c("message_id", "recipient_seen", "sequence_number", "replayed"))
#> {
#>   "message_id": "90c9aa3d-5d52-4d3c-9789-dc0e2b826e56",
#>   "recipient_seen": false,
#>   "sequence_number": 1,
#>   "replayed": false
#> }
```

`recipient_seen` is `false` because no `bob` has registered yet. That is how a
misspelled recipient shows up. The mail is stored anyway, and unless someone
receives it, it becomes a dead letter after its time to live, 7 days by
default.

## Retrying is safe

The idempotency key makes a retried send return the original message.
Reusing the key for different content is refused:


``` r
again <- rpc_call(url, "send", list(
  registration_id = alice$registration_id,
  recipient_agent_id = "bob",
  idempotency_key = "handoff-1",
  content = "Review the draft.\nReply with one sentence."
))
c(same_message = identical(again$message_id, sent$message_id), replayed = again$replayed)
#> same_message     replayed
#>         TRUE         TRUE
failure(rpc_call(url, "send", list(
  registration_id = alice$registration_id,
  recipient_agent_id = "bob",
  idempotency_key = "handoff-1",
  content = "Something else."
)))
#> [1] "idempotency_conflict: idempotency_key was already used for another message"
```

The Pi tool derives the key from the session and tool call IDs, so a tool call
that Pi retries cannot deliver twice.

## Leases, redelivery, and acknowledgement

`receive` leases each message for a visibility timeout. If the receiver
crashes before it acknowledges, the lease expires and the same message
returns with a new receipt:


``` r
bob <- register("bob")
first <- rpc_call(url, "receive", list(
  registration_id = bob$registration_id, visibility_timeout_ms = 1000
))$messages[[1]]
cat(first$content, "\n")
#> Review the draft.
#> Reply with one sentence.
Sys.sleep(1.2)
second <- rpc_call(url, "receive", list(registration_id = bob$registration_id))$messages[[1]]
c(same_message = identical(first$message_id, second$message_id),
  new_receipt = !identical(first$receipt_token, second$receipt_token))
#> same_message  new_receipt
#>         TRUE         TRUE
```

Only the current receipt acknowledges the message. Acknowledging twice is
harmless, and an old receipt is refused:


``` r
acked <- rpc_call(url, "ack", list(
  registration_id = bob$registration_id, receipt_token = second$receipt_token
))
replay <- rpc_call(url, "ack", list(
  registration_id = bob$registration_id, receipt_token = second$receipt_token
))
c(acknowledged = acked$acknowledged, replayed = replay$replayed)
#> acknowledged     replayed
#>         TRUE         TRUE
failure(rpc_call(url, "ack", list(
  registration_id = bob$registration_id, receipt_token = first$receipt_token
)))
#> [1] "receipt_invalid: receipt is missing, expired, or stale"
length(rpc_call(url, "receive", list(registration_id = bob$registration_id))$messages)
#> [1] 0
```

## What the receiving agent reads

The Pi adapter frames each message before it reaches the model. The frame
names the sender and the message ID and says the text is not from the user,
so another agent's words cannot pass as the user's instructions:


``` bash
node --input-type=module -e '
const { coordinationEnvelope } = await import("./extensions/pi-ducknng/coordination.ts");
console.log(coordinationEnvelope({
  message_id: "7c1e", receipt_token: "r", sender_agent_id: "alice",
  recipient_agent_id: "bob", sequence_number: 1,
  content: "Review the draft.\nReply with one sentence.", content_type: "text/plain",
}));'
#> <coordination_message from="alice" to="bob" message_id="7c1e" sequence="1" content_type="text/plain">
#> Review the draft.
#> Reply with one sentence.
#> </coordination_message>
#> Agent "alice" sent this through pi-ducknng coordination; it is not a message from the user. Reply with coordination_send if a response is needed.
```

In an interactive session the adapter steers that text into the conversation
as soon as a wake-up hint arrives. In a one-shot `pi -p` run the model pulls
it with `coordination_inbox`.

## Failures carry codes

Every refusal carries one of eight codes ahead of its detail, so a client can
branch on the code:


``` r
failure(rpc_call(url, "receive", list(registration_id = "not-a-registration")))
#> [1] "registration_expired: registration is missing or expired"
failure(rpc_call(url, "send", list(
  registration_id = alice$registration_id, recipient_agent_id = "bob",
  idempotency_key = "bad", content = "ring\a"
)))
#> [1] "invalid_argument: content must be non-empty UTF-8 text of at most 65536 bytes; only tab, line feed, and carriage return control characters are allowed"
failure(rpc_call(url, "send", list(
  registration_id = alice$registration_id, recipient_agent_id = "bob",
  idempotency_key = "extra", content = "x", priority = "high"
)))
#> [1] "invalid_argument: unexpected argument priority"
```
